title: Scaling Sub-15ms Spatial Dispatch in Dense Metros

# Scaling Sub-15ms Spatial Dispatch in Dense Metros

High-density metropolitan logistics demand real-time synchronization between supply nodes and dynamic consumer intent. Traditional geospatial queries using standard relational spatial extensions struggle under peak loads where millions of concurrent state transitions occur every second.

At Zugado Technologies, our engineering team tackled this constraint by designing a deterministic zero-spill spatial coordination architecture capable of sub-15ms dispatch SLAs.

---

## The Bottleneck in Traditional Spatial R-Trees

Standard R-Trees and spatial databases suffer from lock contention during rapid cluster boundary mutations. When thousands of vehicles cross micro-cell boundaries simultaneously, boundary re-balancing introduces cascading lock wait states.

```
[Dynamic Request] ──> [Cell Boundary Mutation] ──> Lock Wait (>45ms)
```

To eliminate this, we decoupled indexing from persistent storage:

1. **Fixed Discrete Global Hexagonal Cells**: Pre-tessellated hierarchical spatial indices.
2. **Memory-Mapped Lock-Free Ring Buffers**: Utilizing CPU atomic primitives for concurrent spatial state ingestion.
3. **Deterministic Cluster Partitioning**: Ensuring calculations stay strictly bounded to local micro-cells without cross-zone latency amplification.

---

## Zero-Spill Geometric Partitioning

By ensuring zero-spill geometric bounds, local traffic disruptions or localized demand surges in one district never impact adjacent cluster dispatch threads. Each spatial quadrant converges independently within isolated execution boundaries.

### Performance Benchmarks

* **P50 Dispatch Latency**: 4.2ms
* **P99 Dispatch Latency**: 13.8ms
* **Cross-Partition Contention**: 0.00% under 100,000 req/sec

In our upcoming paper, our research team will share further metrics on WebAssembly edge acceleration.

title: Deterministic CRDT Synchronization on Ephemeral Edge Topologies

# Deterministic CRDT Synchronization on Ephemeral Edge Topologies

In decentralized applied research at Zugado Labs, our experimental initiatives explore resilient communication protocols across intermittently connected edge networks.

When edge devices participate in spatial consensus without round-trip access to central datacenters, standard Paxos or Raft consensus models become impractical due to connection dropouts.

---

## Operation-Based vs State-Based CRDTs

State-based conflict-free replicated data types (CvRDTs) transmit full state payload during gossip synchronization, creating excessive bandwidth utilization on mobile networks. 

Zugado Labs designed a custom **delta-mutation delta-CRDT engine**:

* **Delta-State Accumulators**: Transmits only causal mutation deltas.
* **Deterministic Lamport Vectors**: Resolves concurrency ordering without wall-clock skew vulnerabilities.
* **WebAssembly Edge Sandbox**: Sandbox execution overhead stays below 0.3ms per mutation.

```rust
// Rust delta-state representation
pub struct SpatialVectorDelta {
    pub cell_id: u64,
    pub mutation_vector: u64,
    pub state_hash: [u8; 32],
}
```
